thread:
Anna: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — wanted to capture a few process clarifications that came up about releases / oncall / quality bars / SLAs. Ask here and we'll answer live.

Leah: Thanks! First Q — what's the new release cadence again? Monthly minors + weekly patches?

Mike: Short answer: weekly patch releases (bugfix/security), monthly minor releases (features, opt-ins), quarterly major milestones (platform changes). Weeklies: Tue 10:00 PT deploy window. Monthlies: 2nd Tue of month. Quarters: roadmap-aligned.

Kai: Exceptions for hotfixes: any critical security/availability issue can go out immediately after a signed-off emergency review (sigs in #eng-sre). Use `rdeploy emergency --short-circuit` and ping @mike.

Sasha: On oncall — rotation is 1 week for primary, 2 week for secondary. Primary is for pages; secondary for ticket triage and paged escalation. If primary is OOO open a shift swap in the schedule doc.

Jordan: Runbooks: canonical runbooks live in /docs/oncall/runbooks (link: https://redwood/internal/runbooks). Add a short checklist for any new service before it ships: alerting, runbook, kill-switch, perf budget.

Anna: Quality bar: minimums before we accept to monthly: unit tests passing, integration smoke passing, basic performance gate (p95 < configured). Also require a prompt-set regression check for LLM models — no obvious output regressions on canary set.

Kai: Concretely: CI gates = unit+lint -> integration smoke -> canary deploy (5% traffic for 24h) -> gradual rollout. If any failure in canary, auto-rollback.

Leah: How are SLAs defined per product tier?

Mike: Hosted API: SLO is 99.5% availability, enterprise SLAs negotiate to 99.9%/99.95% with credits. Dedicated customers get contractual SLAs tied to capacity. All SLAs have error budgets and runbook playbooks.

Sasha: Error budget policy: when an SLO burns > 50% in a month, we pause all non-critical feature rollouts and convene a postmortem review. ops-bridge will create the ticket.

Anna: Where do release owners live? Each release (monthly/minor) needs an owner listed in the release doc — primary engineer + release manager. Create a release ticket in JIRA with 'release-owner' tag.

Jordan: For Private deployments, we do staged packaging + canary in staging cluster identical to customer infra, then coordinate customer cutover windows. Expect longer lead times.

Kai: A few tactical notes from eng: make sure new services ship with `metrics:request_latency`, `metrics:error_rate`, and `feature_flag:kill_switch`. Small YAML snippet:

``nobservability:
  metrics:
    - request_latency
    - error_rate
feature_flags:
  kill_switch: true
```

Leah: Question: are there stricter quality bars for models?

Mike: Yes — model promos need offline eval pass, golden-prompt regression < threshold, and an embedding drift check.

Anna: If you have follow-ups add them here. We'll capture answers into the process playbook and link in the handbook. Thanks — we'll update the runbook and ping when fields are live. :white_check_mark:
